fix(demo): both exporters drain one recording buffer; label the API break

`exportText` and `exportHtml` both default `clear: true` and both read
`Console._recorded`, so the dual-export path added in the previous commit
wrote the second file from an already-emptied buffer — silently, exit 0.
Verified by reverting the fix: EXPORT_TEXT landed at 0 bytes.

Passing `{ clear: false }` on every save rather than on all-but-the-last
keeps the loop position-independent; nothing needs the buffer cleared
because the process exits immediately after.

`@promptctl/rich-js` is published at 0.7.0, so removing barrel exports
without a version signal would ship a break under a patch. Bumped to
0.8.0 — pre-1.0 semver's breaking-change slot — via the
`npm version minor --no-git-tag-version` step publish.yml documents.

Three comment counts dropped rather than corrected: "(all 17)" box
variants, "four members" on WidgetBase's abstracts, and EXPORT_HTML named
as the recording trigger. A count beside the list it counts is a second
representation of one fact and rots on the next addition; naming the
members and deferring the env-var list to the bootstrap cannot.

docs(coverage): describe the value/type evidence split in CLAUDE.md

The gate section still described one question asked of every export and an
allowlist that was burndown debt. Both are now wrong. Rewritten to teach the
decision a future agent actually faces: adding a value export is two changes,
adding a type export is usually one, and the allowlist is a permanent
exemption list whose second entry should feel like a big deal.

Also adds a smoke test for the rich-explore coverage renderer. It demonstrates
a dozen exports with no narrative demo of their own and is reachable only by
pressing 'c' inside the TUI, so the Playwright first-frame check never reaches
it — a renderer that throws would have stayed silent until a user pressed the
key.

feat(coverage): hold types to reachability, values to demos (rich-coverage-0as.1)

The demo-coverage gate asked every public export one question — "is this
name in an import statement under examples/?" — and 74 of the 102 exports
in the allowlist could not answer it. `visitImports` only walks import
declarations, and idiomatic TypeScript never names a type-only export:
options arrive as object literals, aliases as bare values, structural
interfaces inline. Clearing those entries could only ever mean writing
`import type { PanelOptions }` plus an annotation read by nobody.

So each origin now carries an `ExportKind` discriminator, and the kind
decides which evidence counts — once, where the universe is partitioned,
not branched through the invariants. A value is demonstrated by a demo
naming it. A type is demonstrated by `collectTypeClosure`: reachable
through type positions from a demonstrated value, which is exactly the
condition under which changing it breaks `examples/`. The type check is
derived from the value check rather than parallel to it — demonstrate the
class and its options type follows.

Deleted from the public API: the five TextInput cursor helpers in
core/cells (`asCodeUnit`, `cellFitFrom`, `cellColToCodeUnitOffset`,
`nextCodePoint`, `prevCodePoint` — one consumer, no docs, siblings all
covered); `Tag`, the markup tokenizer's token class, which no public
signature takes or returns; and `registerMarkupTag`/`unregisterMarkupTag`,
three-line forwarders to `globalMarkupRegistry`, which is itself exported.

Demonstrated the remaining 19 undemonstrated values in demos that already
existed — no new demo was needed. The kitchen-sink renderer takes 12
(a custom `Box`, the Highlighter family including a subclass, Segment→ANSI,
`Span`, `Spinner`, `Table`+`Column`); dropdown-demo gains a `WidgetBase`
subclass that echoes its `KeyEvent`s and reports `hasOverlay` per widget;
markup-plugins registers on the global registry; template-bindings shows
`createRichTextEngine()`; themes-and-color-studio exports text as well as
HTML, the two writers now being two rows of data rather than two branches.

The allowlist goes from 102 entries to one (`nodeAsk`, which needs
interactive line input every TUI demo cannot give it).

Verified by falsifying all four invariants, not by watching them pass:
dropping the last entry names `nodeAsk (value)`; a public interface
reachable from nothing names `OrphanProbe (type)`; an entry for no real
export is dead; entries for `Panel` and `PanelOptions` are both reported
redundant, proving the check works on either kind. Full suite 1766 green,
lint clean across all three tsc passes, all 10 demo bundles boot in
Playwright.

chore(coverage): retire the Flagship typing from test/coverage/ (rich-demos-l2x.8) (#68)

* chore(coverage): retire the Flagship typing from test/coverage/ (rich-demos-l2x.8)

The five-flagship / source-module-ownership model was repealed by its own
epic and its spec deleted in #66, but it was still encoded in types here:
a `Flagship` string-literal union naming five demos that will not be built,
a `burndown(flagship)` helper, and a discriminated `AllowlistEntry` whose
`permanent` case was never once realized.

Collapse `AllowlistEntry` to `{ reason: string }`. Every entry now carries a
written reason rather than a tag pointing at a repealed plan; the six entries
that already had real notes keep them, reworded to state the cause without
the flagship vocabulary. Regroup by the subsystem each export is *declared*
in — declaration site is what the verifier actually keys coverage on, so it
is the ordering that matches how entries clear.

`coverage.test.ts` loses its branch on the never-varying discriminator and
its "keystone of the epic" framing; what it verifies is a coverage floor,
and whether a demo is any good is judgment no assertion here can carry.

Behavior of the three invariants is unchanged, and verified by falsifying
each one against the new type rather than only watching them pass: dropping
an uncovered entry reports the gap, an entry naming no real export reports
dead, and an entry for an already-demoed export reports redundant.

`grep -rni flagship` now returns nothing outside git history; lint (all
three passes) and the full vitest suite are clean.

* chore(coverage): point the shared untriaged reason at its removal plan

The one reason shared by 96 entries said the absence was untriaged but
named nothing that would ever change that — a justification field with no
addressee. Name rich-coverage-0as.1, the ticket whose end state is a
per-export outcome for each of them.

Not per-export reasons here: that investigation has not happened, and 96
distinct sentences asserting it had would make the file read more
authoritative while being less true.
